Sean —

Sean / Naomi / Elena —

Triage summary: we observe immediate GPU pool "alpha-3" oversubscription in the us-west region. Key points:
- Pool headroom dropped from 28% -> 6% between 08:30–08:48 PT.
- Several model shards for the LLM variant pinned by NovaPay show high KV cache misses leading to amplified compute per request.
- Autoscale failed to reclaim capacity due to a combination of long-running KV-heavy requests and a saturation trigger threshold that didn't detect the pattern.

We attached pool utilization for the last 2 hours and a short error sample (both attached). Preliminary root cause: sustained high tail latency due to cache churn + contention on alpha-3. This caused request queuing and forced our fallback that returns 5xx for timeouts.

Mitigation steps taken (in flight):
1) Temporarily evicted non-critical best-effort workloads from alpha-3 to free ~18% headroom (complete).
2) Promoted NovaPay's reserved instances to a higher-priority slice within the pool (in progress).
3) Increased the per-customer token timeout from 15s -> 25s to reduce spurious 5xx (deployed).

Request to execs / commercial: to prevent recurrence we recommend a one-time burst allocation of 6 gpus in us-west for the next 8 hours and a rollback to normal after noon PT. This will avoid throttling while we push a long-term fix (kv-cache pinning + autoscale threshold tune). Cost/credit impact: ~6 GPU-hours — recommend we approve as a customer reliability credit and avoid SLA credits.

Attachments: pool-usage-20270504.csv (12 KB), error-sample-20270504.txt (3 KB)

I'll continue to monitor and share metrics every 30 minutes.

—Vivek
